summary: Intermittent request hold at API gateway: delayed flush and header accumulation causing late 503s and tail latency spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a pattern of elevated tail latency and some 503 responses for long-running streaming completions. The symptoms show requests accepted by the API gateway but no bytes forwarded to the backend for up to 25s, then a late flush occurs and either a 503 or full completion is returned with a large TTFB. This started after a routing change deployed 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC affecting the dedicated pool for us-west.

Impact:
- Intermittent but reproducible for a subset of customer traffic (ClipperHealth dedicated pool).
- Observed for streaming completions > 8k tokens and for requests that include large client-side trace headers (~>12KB).
- Customer reports user-facing timeouts and degraded UX during peak hours; estimated ~3% of streamed requests in the last 24h.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted: Dedicated capacity for ClippeHealth (us-west).
- APIGW version: apigw-2.6.1 (deployed 2026-03-11).
- Realtime proxy: realtime-proxy-1.3.4.

Observed behavior:
1) Client completes request upload (chunked) and waits for a streaming response.
2) APIGW accepts request, downstream connection to proxy shows no upstream write for 12–25s.
3) APIGW then issues a flush/coalesce write that sends a large header blob; backend interprets as end-of-headers and responds with 503 or occasionally completes but with large TTFB.

Expected behavior:
- APIGW should stream request body to backend as chunks arrive, and not buffer header/metadata beyond configured thresholds. No mid-stream idle should be introduced for healthy streaming completions.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Use ClippeHealth account on dedicated pool in us-west.
2) Send a streaming completion with ~10k token expected output and include x-trace-cookie with several hops (~>12KB header).
3) Observe TTFB and watch APIGW->proxy traces for delayed writes.

Quick logs / traces:
- apigw access (tail): 
  2026-03-12T08:21:44Z GET /v1/stream 200 "chunked" ua=curl/7.85 ttfb_ms=24512
  2026-03-12T08:24:12Z GET /v1/stream 503 "upstream-reset" ua=python-requests/2.31 ttfb_ms=16672
- proxy logs (subset): 
  2026-03-12T08:21:44Z conn=78945 receive-chunk size=512
  2026-03-12T08:21:44Z conn=78945 upstream-write DELAYED by 18000ms (coalescing)
  2026-03-12T08:21:61Z conn=78945 upstream-write flush total-size=12812

Notes: headersize from sample request = 13140 bytes. APIGW configured idle_send_timeout=15s and max_header_size=16KB. The repro indicates buffering triggered around 12–18s, then a large coalesced write was performed.
steps_to_reproduce: Initiate a streamed completion from a client with a large trace header (~>12KB) against the ClippeHealth dedicated pool in us-west.
Ensure request body is sent chunked over several seconds to simulate slow client upload.
Observe APIGW and proxy connection traces; look for delayed upstream-write events and coalesced flushes at ~12-25s.
Compare TTFB and response codes for streamed vs non-streamed requests.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:00 UTC: Reproduced with internal test harness when adding large trace header and slow chunk cadence.

Hypothesis A: APIGW coalescing logic uses idle_send_timeout and a write threshold; with slow client chunking the gateway holds upstream writes until coalescing window expires, leading to backend timeouts and 503s.
Hypothesis B: Recent routing change (apigw-2.6.1) changed the buffer/flush policy; compare with previous version apigw-2.5.x (no incidents reported).
Observability: trace spans show a gap between client upload events and upstream writes. There are corresponding increase in proxy buffer sizes prior to flush.
Temporarily increased idle_send_timeout to 45s in a canary (us-west-canary) and observed a drop in 503s but longer client-facing TTFB; indicates tradeoff but mitigates errors.
Related PRs: github.com/redwood/realtime-proxy/pull/412 modifies coalescing window; github.com/redwood/apigw/pull/789 added a config flag for aggressive coalescing.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:03 - Ava Martinez (Support): Logged after customer escalation. Collected request samples and initial traces. Asked infra to triage routing change rolled 2026-03-11.
2026-03-12 11:10 - SRE on-call (Priya Desai): Confirmed reproduction in staging with large headers and slow chunking. Hypothesis A looks likely. Spun up canary with idle_send_timeout=45s.

2026-03-12 12:55 - Liam Patel (Engineer): Canary shows 4x fewer 503s but TTFB increased median by 300ms. Preparing a safer fix: modify coalescing to be header-size-aware so large headers trigger immediate flush instead of waiting full coalescing window.
2026-03-13 08:22 - Customer (ClippeHealth, ops): Thank you, the canary reduced user-facing errors. They requested a permanent change and a postmortem once fixed.
2026-03-14 09:40 - Liam Patel (Engineer): Draft PR for header-aware flush ready for review. Planning a dedicated-pool rollout with feature flag and monitoring thresholds.
resolution: Mitigated (temporary): increased APIGW idle_send_timeout on canary and affected dedicated pool to reduce 503s. Permanent fix: landed PR to make coalescing header-aware (github.com/redwood/realtime-proxy/pull/412) and updated APIGW config to flush if header accumulation > 10KB. Plan: staged rollout to dedicated pools over 48h with watch thresholds. Postmortem and follow-up on routing change rollback policy scheduled.
resolution_notes: Rollback/mitigation: Applied idle_send_timeout=45s for ClippeHealth dedicated pool at 2026-03-12 13:20 UTC.
Code fix: realtime-proxy patched to check pending header length and flush early; merged 2026-03-14 PR 412.
Rollout: Feature-flagged rollout planned: canary->10%->50%->100% over 48h with SLO checks.
Action items: Update APIGW runbook to include header-size thresholds, add synthetic test for slow-chunk + large headers, and notify customers of fix schedule.
